questions.stem: Who invented the telephone?
questions.explanation: Alexander Graham Bell patented the telephone in 1876. Thomas Edison invented the electric bulb and phonograph; Guglielmo Marconi pioneered radio (wireless telegraphy); Nikola Tesla developed alternating current (AC) systems. Antonio Meucci is also credited by some as an early developer of telephone-like devices.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The discovery of penicillin, the first antibiotic, is credited to:
questions.explanation: Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin in 1928 from the mould Penicillium notatum. He shared the 1945 Nobel Prize in Medicine with Florey and Chain, who developed it into a usable drug. Louis Pasteur developed pasteurisation and vaccines; Robert Koch identified the TB and cholera bacteria; Edward Jenner pioneered the smallpox vaccine.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Who is credited with the invention of the electric light bulb (practical incandescent lamp)?
questions.explanation: Thomas Alva Edison developed the first commercially practical incandescent light bulb in 1879. He held over 1,000 patents, including the phonograph and motion picture camera. Michael Faraday discovered electromagnetic induction; James Watt improved the steam engine; Benjamin Franklin's experiments established the nature of lightning as electricity.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The law of gravitation was formulated by:
questions.explanation: Sir Isaac Newton formulated the law of universal gravitation, published in 'Philosophiae Naturalis Principia Mathematica' (1687), along with the three laws of motion. Einstein later refined gravity with general relativity (1915). Kepler discovered the laws of planetary motion; Galileo pioneered the use of the telescope for astronomy and studied falling bodies.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Who discovered the law of buoyancy (a body immersed in fluid experiences an upthrust equal to the weight of fluid displaced)?
questions.explanation: Archimedes of Syracuse (Greek, 287–212 BCE) discovered the principle of buoyancy ('Eureka!'). He also developed principles of levers and the Archimedes screw. Pascal's law concerns pressure in fluids; Bernoulli's principle relates fluid speed and pressure; Boyle's law relates gas pressure and volume.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The invention of the World Wide Web (WWW) is credited to:
questions.explanation: Tim Berners-Lee, a British computer scientist at CERN, invented the World Wide Web in 1989, creating HTML, HTTP, and the first web browser. Vint Cerf and Bob Kahn developed TCP/IP (the foundational internet protocols) — note the WWW and the Internet are distinct. Bill Gates co-founded Microsoft; Steve Jobs co-founded Apple.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Who discovered radioactivity?
questions.explanation: Henri Becquerel discovered radioactivity in 1896 (in uranium salts). Marie and Pierre Curie expanded the work, discovering polonium and radium and coining the term 'radioactivity'; all three shared the 1903 Nobel Prize in Physics. Rutherford discovered the atomic nucleus; Wilhelm Roentgen discovered X-rays (1895, first Nobel Physics, 1901).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The Indian scientist who discovered the 'Raman Effect' (scattering of light), winning the 1930 Nobel Prize in Physics, was:
questions.explanation: Sir C.V. Raman discovered the Raman Effect (inelastic scattering of light by molecules) in 1928, winning the 1930 Nobel Prize in Physics — the first Asian to win a Nobel in a science field. National Science Day (28 February) commemorates this discovery. S.N. Bose is known for Bose-Einstein statistics; Meghnad Saha for the Saha ionisation equation; Homi Bhabha is the 'Father of India's nuclear programme'.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Who invented dynamite, and later established the prize bearing his name?
questions.explanation: Alfred Nobel, a Swedish chemist, invented dynamite in 1867. Troubled by his invention's destructive use, he bequeathed his fortune to establish the Nobel Prizes (first awarded 1901) in Physics, Chemistry, Medicine, Literature, and Peace (Economics added in 1969). Antoine Lavoisier is the 'Father of Modern Chemistry'.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The structure of the DNA double helix was discovered by:
questions.explanation: James Watson and Francis Crick described the double-helix structure of DNA in 1953, using X-ray crystallography data from Rosalind Franklin and Maurice Wilkins. Watson, Crick, and Wilkins shared the 1962 Nobel Prize. Mendel founded genetics; Thomas Hunt Morgan established the chromosomal theory of inheritance using fruit flies.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Who developed the polio vaccine (injectable, inactivated) in 1955?
questions.explanation: Jonas Salk developed the first effective injectable (inactivated) polio vaccine, announced in 1955. Albert Sabin later developed the oral polio vaccine (OPV), which became widely used in mass-immunisation campaigns. Salk famously did not patent his vaccine, saying 'Could you patent the sun?'. Edward Jenner pioneered the smallpox vaccine.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The jet engine was invented by:
questions.explanation: Sir Frank Whittle, a British RAF engineer, patented the turbojet engine in 1930 and ran the first successful test in 1937 (German Hans von Ohain developed one independently around the same time). The Wright Brothers achieved the first powered flight (1903); Igor Sikorsky pioneered the helicopter; Karl Benz built the first practical automobile.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Who proposed the theory of relativity (special and general)?
questions.explanation: Albert Einstein proposed special relativity (1905, E=mc²) and general relativity (1915, gravity as spacetime curvature). He won the 1921 Nobel Prize, but for the photoelectric effect (not relativity). Max Planck founded quantum theory; Niels Bohr modelled the atom; Heisenberg formulated the uncertainty principle — all pillars of modern physics.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The discovery of the electron is credited to:
questions.explanation: J.J. Thomson discovered the electron in 1897 through cathode-ray experiments, winning the 1906 Nobel Prize. Ernest Rutherford discovered the proton and the nucleus (gold-foil experiment); James Chadwick discovered the neutron (1932). Together these built the modern atomic model. Thomson proposed the 'plum pudding' model, later revised by Rutherford and Bohr.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Who invented the World's first programmable general-purpose computer concept (the Analytical Engine)?
questions.explanation: Charles Babbage designed the Analytical Engine (1837), a mechanical general-purpose computer, earning him the title 'Father of the Computer'. Ada Lovelace wrote the first algorithm intended for it, making her arguably the first programmer. Alan Turing formalised computation (Turing machine); John von Neumann developed the stored-program architecture used in modern computers.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The vaccine for smallpox was pioneered by:
questions.explanation: Edward Jenner pioneered the smallpox vaccine in 1796, using cowpox material (the word 'vaccine' comes from 'vacca', Latin for cow). This was the first successful vaccine and laid the foundation for immunology. Smallpox was declared eradicated by the WHO in 1980 — the only human disease so far eradicated. Pasteur later developed vaccines for rabies and anthrax.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Who is credited with inventing the radio (wireless telegraphy), winning the 1909 Nobel Prize in Physics?
questions.explanation: Guglielmo Marconi developed practical wireless telegraphy (radio) and won the 1909 Nobel Prize in Physics (shared with Karl Braun). Heinrich Hertz first demonstrated electromagnetic waves (the unit Hz is named after him); Nikola Tesla's patents on radio were later recognised by the US Supreme Court (1943). The Indian scientist Jagadish Chandra Bose also made pioneering contributions to radio waves.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The periodic table of elements was devised by:
questions.explanation: Dmitri Mendeleev published the periodic table in 1869, arranging elements by atomic mass and leaving gaps for undiscovered elements (whose properties he predicted accurately). John Dalton proposed modern atomic theory; Lavoisier compiled the first list of elements and is the 'Father of Modern Chemistry'; Boyle pioneered the concept of chemical elements.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Who invented the steam engine that powered the Industrial Revolution (the improved version with a separate condenser)?
questions.explanation: James Watt dramatically improved the steam engine in 1769 by adding a separate condenser, vastly increasing efficiency — a key driver of the Industrial Revolution. The unit of power, the 'watt', is named after him. Thomas Newcomen built the earlier atmospheric engine; George Stephenson built the first practical steam locomotive ('Rocket'); Arkwright pioneered factory-based textile spinning.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The discovery that the Earth revolves around the Sun (heliocentric model) is associated with:
questions.explanation: Nicolaus Copernicus proposed the heliocentric model (Sun at centre) in 'De revolutionibus orbium coelestium' (1543), overturning Ptolemy's geocentric (Earth-centred) model. Galileo's telescope observations and Kepler's laws later supported it. Tycho Brahe made precise observations used by Kepler; Edmond Halley predicted the return of the comet now named after him.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which scientist discovered the neutron, completing the picture of the atomic nucleus?
questions.explanation: James Chadwick discovered the neutron in 1932, winning the 1935 Nobel Prize. The neutron's discovery explained isotopes and made nuclear fission possible. J.J. Thomson found the electron; Rutherford the proton. Wolfgang Pauli predicted the neutrino; Enrico Fermi built the first nuclear reactor and contributed to neutron physics.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The Indian-American scientist Har Gobind Khorana won the 1968 Nobel Prize in Medicine for work related to:
options: Interpreting the genetic code and protein synthesis
questions.explanation: Har Gobind Khorana (born in undivided India, later US citizen) shared the 1968 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine with Marshall Nirenberg and Robert Holley for interpreting the genetic code and its function in protein synthesis. He later achieved the first chemical synthesis of a gene. The Human Genome Project was a much later (2003) collaborative effort.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Who formulated the laws of planetary motion, establishing that planets move in elliptical orbits?
questions.explanation: Johannes Kepler formulated three laws of planetary motion (1609–1619): (1) planets move in ellipses with the Sun at one focus; (2) a line from Sun to planet sweeps equal areas in equal times; (3) the square of the orbital period is proportional to the cube of the semi-major axis. He used Tycho Brahe's precise data. Newton later explained these via gravitation.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The process of vulcanisation of rubber (making it durable and elastic) was discovered by:
questions.explanation: Charles Goodyear discovered vulcanisation (heating rubber with sulphur) in 1839, making rubber durable and weather-resistant. John Dunlop invented the pneumatic tyre; Leo Baekeland invented Bakelite (the first synthetic plastic, 1907); Wallace Carothers invented nylon and neoprene at DuPont. The Goodyear Tire company is named in his honour (though he had no connection to it).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which discovery by Michael Faraday forms the basis of electric generators and transformers?
questions.explanation: Michael Faraday discovered electromagnetic induction in 1831 — that a changing magnetic field induces an electric current. This principle underlies electric generators, transformers, and most electrical power technology. Faraday's law is a cornerstone of electromagnetism. The photoelectric effect was explained by Einstein; superconductivity was discovered by Kamerlingh Onnes; thermionic emission underlies vacuum tubes.
questions.subject: General Knowledge
